replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig uses sadness belonging to persons rather than brains and thoughts lacking weight or location to distinguish mental from physical properties, challenging reductive materialism and preserving an immaterial personal cause. Principal limitation: These contrasts establish neither substance dualism nor disembodied agency and exclude neither nonreductive physicalism nor emergence, leaving the ontological transition unsupported. Live burden: Craig must derive an existing immaterial self and connect its agency to the universe’s cause, while Flew must explain why personhood requires embodiment despite irreducible mentality. Locked score: Exact 66 reflects logical coherence 64 and evidence warrant 60 for incomplete inference, responsiveness 68 and relevance and burden 71 for addressing one causal attribute, precision and clarity 79 for examples, and calibration and charity 63 for overstating their reach.

Strongest feature: Flew infers that inability to identify a cause earlier than Big Bang warrants agnosticism, treating physics as comparison while avoiding the claim that ignorance proves no cause. Principal limitation: He identifies no physical barrier and never establishes that physical explanation’s stopping point bounds metaphysical inference, so “the end of human knowledge” exceeds his evidence. Live burden: Flew must show why causal reasoning loses warrant beyond physics, while Craig must demonstrate its reliability where empirical access, physical theory, and temporal concepts may fail. Locked score: Exact 77 reflects logical coherence 79 for caution, evidence warrant 61 for an asserted boundary, responsiveness 80 and relevance and burden 85 for confronting Craig, precision and clarity 76 for excessive breadth, and calibration and charity 84 for tentative agnosticism.
